_doc: IDEA-BANK-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-22: the front-door examples must be diverse and actually buildable). Every idea the front door suggests lives here with its domain, reach and the four system-test answers. scripts/build_idea_bank.py runs each one through the seed's own bootstrap stages (read, qualify, instrument) on a generated IDEA.md, refuses the bank when one fails or when the domains are not diverse, and writes site/idea-bank-data.js, which site/suggest.js and site/interview.js read. DEPTH-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-22: 'the depth of idea, the depth of concept of Unlearn and Practical Solutions'): every idea also names its depth: the corpus it keeps growing, the method that makes it trustworthy, and why a reader comes back. A one-trick idea (a single feed, a single alert) has no corpus and is refused. Edit this file, never the generated one. PUBLIC-GOOD-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-22: 'This is about some kind of bigger good, some kind of public good, something that empowers change ... Go get Squarespace if you want e-commerce'): every idea names the change it empowers (`empowers`); domains in `refused_domains` (selling, shops, orders, cost cutting) are refused. WORLDWIDE-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-22: 'these ideas have to work worldwide ... if you don't have the data to back them up, they're not going to work ... point and click and get running'): every idea lists `data`, the worldwide open sources it runs on (or `own`, the user's own records, which exist anywhere); a source with a probe URL is fetched by `build_idea_bank.py --live` (weekly in scout.yml) and an idea whose sources stop answering is retired. GROW-1: `build_idea_bank.py --grow` asks the model route for a new idea each pass, admits it only through the same gates, and retires the oldest beyond `max_active`, so the set never goes static. One rule with DEPTH-1 for apps: build_idea_bank.py calls foundation/ideas.py depth() on every idea (thesis, corpus, loop, returns, hook, public_good, horizon), mapping depth.method to loop and empowers to public_good. BREADTH-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-25, who widened 'a replication ledger for a field' to 'an encyclopedic replication ledger across many fields'): `owner_edits` keeps each edit the owner made to a suggestion with its lesson; --grow shows them to the model as the taste to follow, and an idea whose text holds one of `narrow_phrases` is refused. Text limit is `max_text`.

ideas.text: A living atlas of what works in public policy: programmes graded by their published trials, re-graded when new trials land
ideas.keywords: policy government programme evidence trials what works social public research
ideas.loop: new trials and reviews found weekly, each programme's grade revised, readers' questions turned into new entries
ideas.measure: programmes whose evidence was checked in the last 30 days, target all
ideas.upkeep: trials publish every week and programmes are renamed, scaled up or cut

depth.corpus: hundreds of programmes across housing, health, justice and education, each with its trials
depth.method: grades by study design, shown honestly, with where the evidence is thin
depth.returns: grades move as evidence lands, so a policy reader checks before each decision

ideas.empowers: lets voters, staff and journalists hold programmes to what the evidence shows
ideas.thesis: Many popular public programmes do not do what people believe, and the trials can say which ones do
ideas.hook: Guess whether a famous programme worked, then see what its trials found
horizon: Grade the best-known programmes that have published trials
Re-grade each programme when a new trial or review lands
Add policy areas as their trial evidence is collected

ideas.text: A replication ledger across psychology, medicine and economics: which landmark findings held up when repeated
ideas.keywords: research replication science psychology findings papers evidence academic medicine economics many fields encyclopedia
ideas.loop: new replications found weekly, each finding's standing updated, citing papers flagged when a finding falls
ideas.measure: findings whose standing was checked in the last 30 days
ideas.upkeep: replications and reanalyses publish every week

depth.corpus: landmark findings across psychology, medicine, economics and more, each with every replication attempt
depth.method: standing set by replication size and quality, with the reasoning shown
depth.returns: textbooks and talks keep citing findings whose standing has moved

ideas.empowers: stops shaky findings from steering policy and teaching
ideas.thesis: A large share of famous findings did not hold up when repeated, yet they are still taught and cited
ideas.hook: Guess whether a textbook finding survived replication, then see the record
horizon: Ledger the best-known findings that have a published replication
Flag papers and courses that still cite failed findings
Add each field as its replication data becomes available

ideas.text: An evidence encyclopedia of popular beliefs that studies contradict, each source graded by study design
ideas.keywords: beliefs myths evidence encyclopedia debunking education psychology policing learning
ideas.loop: every hour sources are resolved to DOIs and new systematic reviews are searched for each entry; entries are queued for re-grading when reviews pile up
ideas.measure: share of entries whose evidence was checked within 7 days, target all
ideas.upkeep: new reviews and trials publish every week, links and DOIs rot, and entries need re-grading

depth.corpus: popular beliefs in six topics, each with its graded sources and what works instead
depth.method: every source graded by study design (strong, moderate, mixed, limited), grade shown on the entry
depth.returns: entries are re-graded as reviews land, so a teacher or journalist can cite the current reading

ideas.empowers: gives teachers, journalists and policy staff a cited, graded summary to point people to
ideas.thesis: Telling people they are wrong rarely changes a mind; starting from why a belief feels true does better
ideas.hook: Guess what the evidence says about a common belief, then see the graded sources
horizon: Cover the beliefs already in the six topics
Re-grade entries as new reviews publish
Add beliefs readers ask about most

idea.text: A regional food-system map: farms, food banks, prices and gaps, used every week to route surplus to where it is short
idea.keywords: food bank farms surplus hunger prices region supply charity community
idea.loop: listings and prices refreshed weekly, gaps computed, surplus offers matched to shortfalls and the match followed up
idea.measure: surplus offered that reached a food bank within 48 hours
idea.upkeep: farms, prices and needs change every week

depth.corpus: every farm, food bank and pantry in a region with stock, hours and needs
depth.method: each listing confirmed at its source on a schedule; unconfirmed rows are marked
depth.returns: new surplus and new shortfalls every week

idea.empowers: gets surplus food to people who are short of it
idea.thesis: Food goes to waste a few miles from people who are short of it because nobody can see both at once
idea.hook: See on a map where surplus sits today and which pantry nearby is running short
horizon: Map farms and food banks in one region
Match surplus offers to shortfalls every week
Publish the routing so any region can run it on open map data

idea.text: A claim tracker that follows viral claims, links each to its evidence and updates the verdict when evidence moves
idea.keywords: misinformation fact check claims news viral evidence media truth
idea.loop: new claims picked up daily, matched to existing entries or opened, verdicts revised when new evidence appears
idea.measure: verdicts revised within 7 days of new evidence
idea.upkeep: new claims appear every day and old ones resurface

depth.corpus: a growing graph of claims, their variants and the evidence on each
depth.method: verdicts graded by evidence strength, with what would change them
depth.returns: the same claims come back in new forms, and the record follows them

idea.empowers: lets anyone check a claim before passing it on

data.name: Google Fact Check Tools (ClaimReview, worldwide fact-checkers)

idea.thesis: Viral claims outrun their corrections because nobody tracks a claim across all its variants
idea.hook: Paste something you saw shared and see its whole history and the evidence on it
horizon: Track claims already checked by fact-checkers worldwide
Link variants into one graph and follow re-sharing
Warn readers when a claim they checked comes back changed

idea.text: An atlas of climate adaptation: which flood, heat and drought measures worked where, graded by what happened after
idea.keywords: climate adaptation flood heat drought resilience city environment evidence
idea.loop: case studies and evaluations gathered monthly, each measure re-graded, cities' questions answered from the atlas
idea.measure: measures with an outcome evaluation attached
idea.upkeep: new projects and evaluations every month

depth.corpus: measures from cities worldwide with their costs and measured results
depth.method: results graded by evaluation design; untested claims are marked as such
depth.returns: each season's floods and heatwaves add evidence, so councils check again before every budget

idea.empowers: helps towns spend scarce money on measures that protect people
idea.thesis: Towns copy flood and heat measures that sound good without knowing which ones actually protected people
idea.hook: Pick your town's risk and see which measures elsewhere really cut the damage
horizon: Gather evaluated measures for floods
Add heat and drought, graded by outcome
Help any council shortlist measures by cost and evidence

idea.text: A model evaluation harness that re-tests every new AI model release against its own history
idea.keywords: model evaluation benchmark regression ai release llm
idea.loop: each release run through the same tests, scores compared with history, regressions filed
idea.measure: regressions found before a release is adopted
idea.upkeep: models and providers release new versions every month

depth.corpus: a growing suite of tests and every score every model has had
depth.method: fixed tests, repeated runs and published variance
depth.returns: every new model release is a new comparison against the whole history of scores

idea.empowers: gives the public an independent record of how AI models really behave
idea.thesis: Claims about AI models drift from what the models actually do from release to release
idea.hook: Pick two models and see how they really compare on the same tests over time
horizon: Run a fixed public test suite on each release
Track regressions and publish variance
Let anyone add a test that runs on every future release

idea.text: A free open curriculum that rewrites each lesson from where learners actually get stuck
idea.keywords: curriculum education learning lessons school students teachers course open
idea.loop: learner answers read after each unit, the lesson with the most stuck points rewritten, the change measured on the next cohort
idea.measure: share of learners who pass each unit's check, target rising per cohort
idea.upkeep: every cohort shows new stuck points

depth.corpus: a full course of lessons, exercises and the record of where people stumbled
depth.method: each rewrite is an experiment kept only if the next cohort does better
depth.returns: learners move unit by unit, and teachers reuse it every term

idea.empowers: gives any learner a free course that keeps getting better
idea.thesis: Courses stay the same while learners keep getting stuck at the same places year after year
idea.hook: Take a two-minute check and see the lesson rewritten for exactly where you got stuck
horizon: Publish one full course with a stuck-point record
Rewrite lessons from each cohort's results
Open the method so any teacher can run it on their own course

idea.text: A website for our club or association that learns what brings members back and grows the features they use
idea.keywords: club association website members community society group sports events
idea.loop: visits, sign-ups and event turnout read weekly, the feature or page members use least improved, turnout read again
idea.measure: members who return each month and event turnout
idea.upkeep: events, members and season plans change all year

depth.corpus: years of events, members' turnout and what each change to the site did
depth.method: each change is predicted and kept only if return visits or turnout rose
depth.returns: members come back for every event, and the club's record keeps growing

idea.empowers: keeps volunteer-run community groups alive and growing

data.name: own
data.note: the club's own first-party, cookieless site analytics

idea.thesis: Volunteer-run groups fade because nobody can see what actually brings members back
idea.hook: See this month's turnout and which change last month brought people back
horizon: Run the club's site with turnout tracking
Test one change a month and keep what works
Share what works across clubs of the same kind

idea.text: An impact ledger for a charity that links every programme to its outcomes and shows funders what each donation changed
idea.keywords: charity nonprofit impact outcomes funders donors programme evaluation
idea.loop: programme data read monthly, outcomes recomputed, the weakest programme flagged with what similar charities do
idea.measure: programmes with a measured outcome, target all
idea.upkeep: programmes, people served and funders change every year

depth.corpus: every programme, its spend and the outcomes it produced over the years
depth.method: outcomes compared with a baseline, uncertainty stated
depth.returns: each reporting cycle and funding round draws on it

idea.empowers: moves donations toward what actually helps people
idea.thesis: Donations follow stories more than outcomes because outcomes are rarely shown plainly
idea.hook: See what a single donation changed, in numbers, for a real programme
horizon: Link one charity's programmes to outcomes
Compare against similar charities' published results
Give funders a live view of outcomes instead of annual reports

idea.text: A funding atlas for small charities: every open call, how well it fits and a drafted answer, kept current
idea.keywords: grants funding proposals deadlines nonprofit fundraiser charity
idea.loop: funder pages read weekly, matching calls filed with a draft, outcomes recorded to sharpen the fit score
idea.measure: matching calls missed before their deadline, target 0
idea.upkeep: funders open and close calls all year

depth.corpus: every funder and call, with past awards and what won
depth.method: fit scored from past awards; drafts reuse answers that succeeded
depth.returns: new calls open every week, and each charity's past wins sharpen its next match

idea.thesis: Small charities miss funding they qualify for because finding and answering calls takes staff they do not have
idea.hook: See the open calls your charity fits today, each with a drafted answer
horizon: Index every open call in one country
Score fit from past awards and draft answers

idea.text: A decision journal that records each big choice, its reasons and how it turned out, and learns what I misjudge
idea.keywords: decisions journal personal reflection choices life habits memory
idea.loop: each decision logged with a prediction, revisited when it resolves, my blind spots summarised quarterly
idea.measure: share of predictions that came true, per quarter

depth.corpus: years of my own decisions, predictions and outcomes

depth.returns: every new choice is checked against my own track record

data.note: the person's own decisions and predictions

idea.thesis: People repeat the same misjudgements because they never score their past predictions
idea.hook: Write down one decision and a prediction, and get asked how it turned out later
horizon: Log decisions with predictions
Score them as they resolve
Show the person their own patterns of misjudgement

idea.keywords: habits sleep fitness personal experiments health log routine
idea.loop: one change tried for two weeks, the measure compared with the baseline, kept or dropped, the next test chosen
idea.measure: experiments that measurably helped, per quarter

depth.corpus: every habit I have tried, with its before-and-after numbers
depth.method: baseline, one change at a time, a fixed test window

idea.thesis: Most habit advice is untested for the person following it, and only a personal test can tell
idea.hook: Pick one habit and see your two-week before-and-after numbers
horizon: Run one habit test at a time
Keep only what measurably helped

idea.keywords: open source dependencies packages security maintainers supply chain software
idea.loop: the dependency graph rebuilt weekly, risks scored, fixes proposed to the projects that can make them
idea.measure: high-risk dependencies with a proposed fix
idea.upkeep: new releases and new risks every day

depth.returns: the dependency graph changes with every release, and new risks appear every day

idea.keywords: government contracts procurement tenders corruption spending accountability civic
idea.loop: new tenders and awards read daily, red flags scored, flagged contracts followed to delivery and the flags re-scored
idea.measure: flagged contracts later confirmed as problems, against false flags
idea.upkeep: governments publish new tenders every day

depth.corpus: every published tender, bidder and award in the jurisdictions with open data
depth.method: red flags from published procurement-risk indicators, each shown with its evidence
depth.returns: new contracts every day and a growing record of who won what

idea.empowers: lets citizens and journalists see where public money goes and who gets it
idea.thesis: Rigged public tenders leave patterns in open data that citizens can see if someone looks
idea.hook: See which contracts near you show red flags, and why
horizon: Score red flags on one country's open contracts
Follow flagged contracts to delivery and re-score
Cover every country that publishes open contracting data

owner_edits.before: A replication ledger for a field: which landmark findings held up and which failed, updated as replications publish
owner_edits.after: An encyclopedic replication ledger across many fields: which landmark findings held up and which failed, updated as replications publish
owner_edits.lesson: Rowan liked the idea and widened it from one field to many. Prefer broad, multi-domain, encyclopedic, living versions over single-field ones.

live_example_rule: LIVE-EXAMPLE-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-26: 'make sure you're saying things you will actually build and can actually build ... All product, no pitch. No hyperbole anywhere.'): an idea reaches the front door only with an example: a deployed system on Ultrastable (name, url, https probe, repo registered in doctrine/tenant-repos.json). build_idea_bank.py --check refuses an idea without one; --live fetches each example probe, retires an idea whose example does not answer, and promotes a retired idea whose example now answers. --grow cannot add an idea that has no live example.
